articles.title: Punt FT%: Player Targets
articles.brief: Which players fit a punt FT% build in our 12-team H2H 9-cat league, and how should they be tiered by auction value? Each line must also note the guard stats (AST, 3PTM, ST, PTS) a player brings, because the experts warn that drafting only bad free throw shooters punts four categories.

articles.title: Punt AST: Player Targets
articles.brief: Which players fit a punt AST build, and what does each one give in 3PTM, ST and FT%, the categories that often suffer when you punt assists? The list is short, so the article must say how thin it is and that assists are scarce late and hard to find on waivers.

articles.title: Punt TO: Player Targets
articles.brief: Which high-usage players gain value for us if we ignore turnovers, and how should they be tiered by price? It must explain why experts ignore TO in head-to-head leagues and that streaming for games raises turnovers anyway.

articles.title: Punt 3PTM: Player Targets
articles.brief: Which players fit a punt 3PTM build in our league, grouped into tiers with what each adds in FG%, REB and BLK? It must note that threes are easy to find on waivers, so non-shooters lose less than rankings suggest.

articles.title: Punt FG%: Player Targets
articles.brief: Which players fit a punt FG% build, tiered by value, with their volume in PTS, 3PTM and AST? It must explain why FG% swings week to week and why punting one percentage category works well in head-to-head.

articles.title: Punt ST: Player Targets
articles.brief: Which players fit a punt ST build, and what do they bring in the stable categories? It must explain that steals are among the most variable categories, so they are a sensible punt and a risky thing to pay for.

articles.title: Punt BLK: Player Targets
articles.brief: Which players fit a punt BLK build, and how do they keep us competitive in REB and FG%? It must warn that blocks travel with rebounds and FG%, so chasing only low-block players can sink those two categories too.

articles.title: Breakout Candidates
articles.brief: Which players have the role, usage or minutes growth to finish well above their auction price this season? For each, it must name the opening behind the breakout (departed teammate, bigger role, year-two or year-three step) and which category signals support it.

articles.title: Bust Candidates
articles.brief: Which players are likely to finish below their expected auction price in our 9-cat league, and why (role loss, crowded usage, shooting regression, age)? It must say that a bust label is about price, so each line should give a price at which the player becomes fine to buy.

articles.title: Late-Round Flyers for 1 to 3 USD
articles.brief: Which cheap end-of-auction players have a real path to a role and top 70 upside, so they are worth our last roster spots? Each line must say what has to happen for the flyer to hit and when to drop him if it does not.

articles.title: Injury Risk: Injured, Recovering and Chronic Cases
articles.brief: Which players are injured now, coming back from injury, on minutes limits or load management, or have chronic same-spot lower-body problems? Tiers must separate chronic cases (price down) from one-off injuries (do not overreact), and note who can use one of our 4 IL slots.

articles.title: Shutdown and Trade Risk
articles.brief: Which players could be shut down late in the season or traded before the deadline, and how does that affect their value for our March 28 end? It must flag who matters most for playoff weeks 19 to 21 and which young players could gain if a veteran is moved.

articles.title: Auction Tactics for Our 200 USD Live Draft
articles.brief: How do we run a 200 USD live auction for 12 players in a 12-team league: budget split, a streaming spot, nominations, bidding style, price enforcement and the 1 USD endgame? It must explain why a balanced build beats stars and scrubs at 12 teams, how to read a hot or cold room, and why mock prices and Yahoo prices are only guides.

articles.title: Strategy by Draft Stage: Early, Middle and Late
articles.brief: What should we prioritize in the early, middle and late parts of our auction: stable PTS, REB and AST early, value in the middle tier, and upside flyers at the end? It must cover how the cost of a mistake shrinks further down the board, when to take safe players versus upside, and when position needs start to matter.

articles.title: Do Not Draft by Predicted Injuries, Except Chronic Cases
articles.brief: Why are games played and injury-prone labels poor predictors, and which cases (repeated same-spot lower-body injuries, big men with foot problems, degenerative injuries) should still lower a player's price? It must also cover not stacking several risky players and why injury risk costs more in head-to-head than in roto.

articles.title: Fantasy Playoff Weeks 19 to 21 (Ending 2027-03-28)
articles.brief: How should the playoff schedule for weeks 19, 20 and 21, ending 2027-03-28, affect our draft and our season moves? It must explain that two-game playoff weeks are the factor that matters, that schedule is only a tiebreaker and mostly for early picks, and how to use trades and streaming to gain playoff games later.

articles.title: Two-Game and Five-Game Weeks: Lineup and Streaming Adjustments
articles.brief: How should we adjust daily lineups, streaming adds (max 6 per week) and percentage-category expectations in weeks when a team plays only 2 or as many as 5 games? It must cover why low-volume weeks make FG% and FT% swing, why back-to-back counts matter little except for players returning from injury, and how merged NBA Cup weeks change the count.

articles.title: How to Punt in H2H 9-Cat
articles.brief: When and how should we punt a category in our league, and which categories are good or bad to punt given their stability? It must cover category correlations, why punt rankings mislead, why we should not overpay for punt fits in the auction, and why heavy punting adds variance.

articles.title: Which Categories to Trust: Stability and Winning Margins
articles.brief: Which of our 9 categories are stable (PTS, REB, AST) and which swing a lot (ST, FT%, FG%, BLK), and how should that shape what we pay for? It must explain category correlations, why winning a category needs a big margin, and why threes and steals are easy to find on waivers while assists and points are not.

articles.title: Regression: Shooting, Steals and Blocks
articles.brief: Which shooting and defensive numbers from last season should we expect to move back toward normal, and how do we spot them before paying for them? It must cover regressing FT%, 3P% and 2P% outliers, steal and block conversion rates, and how three-point swings drive in-season buy-low and sell-high calls.

articles.title: Rankings, ADP and Auction Prices: What to Trust in a 9-Cat League
articles.brief: Why are Yahoo ranks, X-rank, ADP and straight 9-cat total rankings unreliable for our H2H 9-cat league, and how do points-league values leak into our draft room? It must show how to use rank versus market price to find value and when a gap between sites is an opportunity.

articles.title: Format Traps: Points-League Players and 9-Cat Fluff
articles.brief: Which players are likely mispriced in our room because their value comes from points-league scoring or from inflated 9-cat totals, and which are undervalued for a category league? Tiers must separate players to avoid at market price from players to target.

articles.title: Price Check: Players Where Sites Disagree
articles.brief: Which players have very different ranks or prices across sources, so their auction price in our room is hard to predict? Each line must say which direction the gap points and at what price the player becomes a buy for us.

articles.title: Sleepers and Expert Targets
articles.brief: Which players do the experts expect to beat their price in our format, tiered by expected cost? Each line must give the reason (overlooked team, role, market overreaction) so we know how far to bid.

articles.title: Bounce-Back Candidates
articles.brief: Which players had a down season from injury, role or a shooting or steals slump and could return to their earlier level? It must explain why one bad season should not set the price and which bounce-backs depend on unstable stats.

articles.title: Safe Core: Players Who Fit Every Build
articles.brief: Which players help in most categories without forcing a punt, so they suit the balanced build recommended for a 12-team auction? Tiers must be by price range, with a note on which stable categories each one provides.

articles.title: Category Specialists: Filling a Need
articles.brief: Which players are strong in one category (PTS, REB, AST, ST, BLK, 3PTM) and could fill a hole late in the auction or in season? It must warn that one-category players look better in punt rankings than they are and should not be bought to fix a category already lost.

articles.title: FG% and FT% Anchors and Liabilities
articles.brief: Which players move our team FG% and FT% most, up or down, given their shot volume? It must note that percentages are team ratios driven by attempts and that FT% is the least stable category year to year.

articles.title: Bigs Who Pass or Shoot Threes
articles.brief: Which big men add assists or threes on top of rebounds and blocks, giving rare category combinations? It must explain why combining categories that do not usually go together carries extra value in H2H.

articles.title: Players with Good or Bad Playoff Schedules
articles.brief: Which players' teams have strong or weak schedules in weeks 19 to 21 ending 2027-03-28, especially two-game weeks? It must say that this list is a tiebreaker between similar players and matters most for expensive players.

articles.title: Handcuffs and Backup Centers
articles.brief: Which backups would step into a big role if the starter ahead of them misses time, and which of them have value on their own? It must explain that in our daily league with 2 bench spots most handcuffs are waiver pickups, not draft stashes.

articles.title: Waiver Watch List
articles.brief: Which undrafted players should we watch in the first weeks for role, minutes or starting changes that make them worth a FAB bid? Each line must state the trigger that would make us add him.

articles.title: Minutes Battles to Watch
articles.brief: Which players are in a fight for minutes or a starting job, and which battles matter for our auction prices? It must note the hedge option of buying both candidates cheaply and cutting the loser, and that a starting job alone does not guarantee minutes.

articles.title: Players on New Teams
articles.brief: Which players changed teams, and is their value likely to rise or fall in the new usage and minutes picture? It must reflect that new-team players often dip in year one unless minutes rise, and flag ripple effects on teammates.

articles.title: Slow Starters: Early-Season Patience and Buy-Low Targets
articles.brief: Which players are likely to start the season slowly (rookies, players after long playoff runs, injury returns) and could be bought low in November trades? It must say how long to hold such players and which ones have early-season value instead.

articles.title: Rookies Worth a Look
articles.brief: Which rookies have a real path to minutes and usage this season, and which belong only in the 1 USD flyer zone or on waivers? It must reflect that most rookie classes give only a few relevant players and that rookie guards usually shoot poorly early.

articles.title: Rookies and Second-Year Players: How to Value Them
articles.brief: How much should we pay for rookies and second-year players, and how long should we hold them in season before cutting? It must cover the year-two jump, year-three breakout odds by price, rookie point guard struggles, the Thanksgiving rule and why Summer League numbers mislead.

articles.title: Projecting Roles: Minutes, Usage and Team Context
articles.brief: How do we project a player's minutes and usage from his team context: crowded rosters, departed or added stars, coaches who lean on starters, deep rotations and positional fit? It must give the order of evidence (minutes, role, usage, production, hype last) and the 240-minute check.

articles.title: Reading Last Season's Numbers in Context
articles.brief: How do we judge last season's stats before paying for them: games with teammates out, late-season tanking stretches, hot streaks, limited-minute samples and Finals hangovers? It must explain single-season myopia in both directions and when to sell a fill-in starter.

articles.title: Streaming and Waivers with FAB and 6 Adds per Week
articles.brief: How should we use our streaming spot, FAB budget and 6 weekly adds to gain games and value in our daily H2H league? It must cover the value of a streaming slot, what to react to early in the season, which categories are easy to stream, and the discovery, optimizing and maximizing phases of the season.

articles.title: Using Our 4 IL Slots and Stashing in a Daily League
articles.brief: When is an injured or backup player worth holding in our daily league with 2 bench and 4 IL slots, and when should we cut him for a streamer? It must explain the new Yahoo IL rules (out players go straight to IL, questionable ones do not) and why most stash advice is for other formats.

articles.title: In-Season Trades Before the 2027-03-04 Deadline
articles.brief: How should we approach trades with experienced managers before the 2027-03-04 deadline: buy low, sell high, 2-for-1 deals and changing our category profile? It must explain why sending out two players for one opens a valuable streaming slot and which hot or cold stretches signal a trade.

articles.title: March Basketball Under the Lottery Reform: Who Rests and Who Plays
articles.brief: Which kinds of teams are likely to rest players, shut down injured players or give young players minutes in March, when our playoffs run? It must explain the expected effect of the anti-tanking lottery reform, teams that do not own their pick, and why late-season numbers from tanking teams should not be trusted.

articles.title: Positions and Centers in a G/G/G/F/F/F/C Roster
articles.brief: How do we cover G, F and C eligibility for daily lineups without reaching for positions, and how should we value centers in our one-C, three-Util roster? It must cover why stats beat positions early, when to check eligibility, and what makes a center worth buying (starting role, about 30 minutes, playing at C rather than PF).

articles.title: Players Returning from Achilles, ACL and Other Major Injuries
articles.brief: What should we expect from players coming back from Achilles tears, ACL tears and other major injuries: timelines, efficiency loss, minutes limits and skipped back-to-backs? It must say how to price them in our H2H league and why the market is often too scared of them.
